builds.howItPlays: You play cheap units like Irresistible Faefolk (2 cost), which can drag an enemy unit along when it moves to a battlefield, and Void Assault, which moves one of your units and then one of theirs, so every fight happens where you choose and against an enemy left on its own. Tricks like Punch First (+5 Might for the turn) win those fights, each win gives Kha'Zix experience to spend on a lasting +1 Might or on pulling a tired unit back to base, and Rengar, Trophy Hunter (a 6-Might unit) can drop straight onto a battlefield where enemies stand, even on your opponent's turn.
builds.whyYou: You like picking your fights: moving your unit in, dragging theirs over, and deciding which enemy stands alone when combat starts. You enjoy the small sums each turn asks for, like which unit to move, whether one trick is enough to win, and when to spend Kha'Zix's experience to save a hurt unit. Your cards do the same job every game, so wins come from your choices more than your draws. If you'd rather win by setting up fights you can't lose than by trading blow for blow, this Kha'Zix suits you.
builds.ratingNotes:
Changed 2026-09-25 (re-rate from the Maintainer's deck picks, style "Void Assault Kha'Zix"). The label stays Midrange. Coordinates move from 5/6/7/6.5 to 6/6.5/7/4 (pace/stance/complexity/variance). The big move is Variance, 6.5 to 4: the old number came from guides that tied luck to drawing the movers, but the scored lists run full playsets and no luck or swing cards. deckListUrl was the bare /decks page and is now sharlie's list. I dropped riftbound.gg from guideUrls because I did not re-read it in this pass. hextechanalytics was re-read: it describes the same Faefolk, Void Assault and Mutating Horror plan.
Scored decks (tools.ts style: Midrange 6/6.5/7/4, mean of 3, labels Midrange x3):
- https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/1ed527e6-b1df-4b60-a685-4e881b542f91 Kha'zix Vendetta post ban (sharlie; 41 likes, guide) Midrange 6.5/6.5/7/4. The scorer suggested Aggro; the rater judged Midrange because many slots go to interaction and flex tricks.
- https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/00615075-422d-4394-8ef7-39db5e45d7ce Kha'Zix Midrange Sett (jarno; 11 likes, pre-ban, x0.75) Midrange 5.5/6/7/4
- https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/e41ee260-bb11-4d3d-84f0-9e5842132988 Kha'Zix (Mainezz; guide, edited post-ban) Midrange 6/6.5/7/4
Adjustments (all three sheets): complexity +1 (the Legend's XP abilities, buff or pull an exhausted unit home, need a target and timing every turn). No Axis had a formula-judgment gap of 2 or more.
Deciding cards:
- Pace: 9 units costing 2 or less (Irresistible Faefolk, Traveling Merchant, Shadow Order Disciple, Kinkou Initiate) against 3 to 6 cards costing 5+ (Rengar, Trophy Hunter, Baron Nashor in jarno's list).
- Stance: about 20 pressure cards against 8 to 9 answers (Star-Crossed, Sabotage, Vex, Apathetic, Hard Bargain, Rampage).
- Complexity: 23 to 25 setup or modes cards (the movers, Void Assault, Grim Resolve, Ride the Wind, Up from the Deep) and 6 to 10 reactive cards (Star-Crossed, Rengar, Mutating Horror's Ambush), plus the Legend.
- Variance: 60 to 68% of cards as 3-ofs, and no luck or swing cards.
Legend ability: when you win a combat, gain 1 XP. Spend 1 XP and exhaust to Buff a unit. Spend 2 XP and exhaust to move an exhausted friendly unit from a battlefield to its base.
Outside labels: sharlie's guide calls the deck "a tempo deck", and the old notes read riftbound.gg and hextechanalytics as Midrange. That is a split, so the label stays Midrange with the unanimous raters.
Also played: Illaoi Tentacles https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/7b410767-964c-4f48-bda9-dc421796799d (Laranj0, Midrange 4.5/5.5/7/5) and https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/f6c4bdbc-6bdf-4d5e-bac6-4a74046170b4 (dantes, 5/5.5/7/5), which ramp into Illaoi and Baron Nashor over tentacle tokens. Untouchable Baron https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/69cc1282-7160-439a-a991-7b931a0095af (Packybara, 5/5.5/7/5.5), which uses Here to Help and Dragonsoul Sage for threats spells can't target. Hidden Evelynn https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/dcb32166-23ef-4362-ab1d-ce981bbeccad (Hartford RQ Best of, June 2026, 6.5/6.5/8/4), which runs three Hidden Evelynn and three Switcheroo.
Confidence: high.
Reviewer check: hextechanalytics' featured list (Demacian Diplomat, First Mate, Qiyana) differs from the scored lists in its flex slots but runs the same engine. Void Assault has no Action or Reaction tag, so the copy keeps it on your own turn.
